coaching.headline: Every Fangtooth, both Primes, ten structures to two, and nobody ever killed Sparrow. A proper fucking mugging.
coaching.team: This was a mugging from first blood to the Core. We took every Fangtooth, both Primes and the Genesis Core, and ten structures to their two. Five of our six won exchanges were followed by an objective or structure, and they never won an exchange at all. The only weak stretch was the early offlane, where Terra kept collecting kills. Everything after that was clean and decisive.

focus.title: Bail out the bleeding lane
focus.action: When one of our laners dies twice to the same opponent before the first Fangtooth, the jungler's next gank goes to that lane.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Sparrow was untouchable and lethal: nine kills, no deaths, and Ikra used as a punching bag four times, starting with first blood. That is a carry doing the fucking job; the zero is now the standard. Damage per minute ran slightly under the usual rate. When Terra is the nearest target, Sparrow shoots past to Ikra, Gideon or Grux if one is safely in range, since every basic attack into Tainted Guard cuts Sparrow's healing.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs turned the jungle into a one-sided hunting trip. Grux died to Feng Mao three times and never got a kill, while Feng Mao led the match in objective damage and the lobby in healing. After ten deaths in the last Feng Mao jungle film, one death here is the real headline. Gideon got it, so when Gideon is alive and in range before a dive, Feng Mao holds Safeguard to eat the comet or meteor first.
perPlayer.093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d: BrEazy's The Fey was the engine of this stomp, and it was not close. More hero damage than anyone in the lobby, no deaths, farm well above the usual pace on the hero, and a hand in more than half our kills. Keep that standard. The next step is making Fly Trap a team call: when it grabs two or more heroes, The Fey calls it in voice so Feng Mao can drop Earth Shatter on the stunned pile.
perPlayer.6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb: Proper support work from KrazyKor88, and none of it needed kills to prove it. Muriel never died, our duo lost nobody early while theirs lost two, and Muriel out-warded Ikra twelve to seven. The Gideon kill came in the exchange shortly before their first tower fell. Next game, when Sparrow picks a target to shoot, Muriel throws Alacrity onto Sparrow first: the shield triggers Exarch, so those shots land faster with bonus magic damage attached. Free damage for one shield.
perPlayer.f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec: RedMxsty's Bayle played two games; the second was far better. Terra treated the early offlane like a fucking buffet: Bayle's first four deaths, three to Terra, came before anyone else on our side had died once. After the fifth, five kills and no deaths, including Grux and Ikra seconds before their inner tower dropped. Next game, after a death to the lane opponent, Bayle takes the next trade only with Dire Howl ready and stays in until its heal lands.

13.5.call: Won 2-0: Bayle killed Grux and Muriel killed Gideon, and their first Outer Tower fell shortly after. The timing does not show who hit the tower or where the other three were.

18.5.call: Won 2-0: Sparrow killed Terra, then The Fey killed Ikra, and we took Mini Prime within the minute while a second exchange, won 2-1, overlapped the take. Kill credits do not show who was at the pit.

23.8.call: Won 2-0: Bayle killed Grux, then Ikra, their Inner Tower fell seconds later and Orb Prime followed. The record does not show who hit the tower or who started Orb Prime.

25.2.call: Won 2-0: Sparrow killed Grux, then Ikra, and their inhibitors and Core fell within ninety seconds. Kill credits do not show who pushed the base.

matchup: Ikra's Narcosis and Genesis plus Drongo's Gag Grenade were the control threat to Sparrow, who has no dash.
The control never produced a kill: Sparrow took first blood on Ikra and our duo had no early deaths.
Terra's Tainted Guard was the enemy item most relevant to an auto-attacker.
build: Grux, their biggest healer, was the obvious healing-cut target, though the record does not show it applied.
It skips the common winning Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra core; nothing shows that cost anything.
eternal: Weald's true-damage volley ignores the armor Terra stacked.
Forage suits a carry who farmed above the usual rate here.
Taproot is the slot-two alternative when Sparrow needs on-hit healing more than burst attack speed.
augment: Endless Hunt resets basic ability cooldowns and adds physical penetration on every takedown.
Nine takedowns gave it plenty to work with; in a game decided by finishing targets, the reset engine fit.
Sun Shards is the common alternative for wave and group damage.
crest: Pacifier is Sparrow's only dash, so it is both the finisher and the exit.
Spending it forward leaves Heightened Senses as the only way out.
No deaths says the exit was never needed at the wrong time.
improvement: Keep the finishing package; short, decisive fights gave no reason to change it.
If Terra's armor stack faces Sparrow in longer fights, compare Sky Splitter against Terminus.
Sky Splitter trades the lifesteal shield for current-health damage; nothing in this match tested that trade.

matchup: Muriel's job was keeping Sparrow out of Ikra's Narcosis, Drongo's Gag Grenade and Grux's pulls and stuns.
Our duo had no early deaths against two for theirs, and Muriel never died.
build: Enra's Blessing shields an immobilized ally, a direct answer to Narcosis and Grux's stuns.
Astral Catalyst shortens the ultimate cooldown on kills and assists; Lifecore heals the lowest-health ally nearby.
It traded the common Marshal, Crystal Tear and Windcaller ally buffs for anti-control protection and ultimate uptime.
eternal: Exarch gives healed or shielded targets attack speed and magical on-hit damage, a natural pairing with Sparrow.
Illumination turns bonus mana regeneration into health regeneration; Fervour heals allies when Muriel basic-attacks heroes.
Revelation, the usual slot-one pick, shortens basic ability cooldowns instead of adding sustain.
augment: Sacrosanct makes Reversal of Fortune drop a Consecrated Ground that buffs allies and damages enemies inside it.
That suits a team that fought around objectives all game.
crest: Tranquility's Grace heals Muriel and nearby heroes; Visionary raises the ward cap.
Muriel placed twelve wards to Ikra's seven and cleared three of the four enemy wards our team destroyed.
Pacifist's diminishing minion gold suits a support leaving the wave to Sparrow.
improvement: Keep the protective core into a lineup with this much control.
If the next enemy team has little immobilization, Crystal Tear in place of Enra's Blessing trades the anti-control shield for output.
This game gave no reason to swap.

matchup: Grux finished with nine deaths, three to Feng Mao, and no kills.
The gank targets that mattered were Terra, who killed Bayle four times, and Gideon, the only enemy to kill Feng Mao.
build: Exactly the winning core; The Perforator has a clear target in Terra's all-armor inventory.
Hero damage ran about a third under Xeebs' usual Feng Mao rate, but these items led the match in objective damage.
That is a role choice, not a build fault.
eternal: Knell shreds both armors with Rust; Frequency and Peal reward opening with the ultimate.
Fracture, the common slot-two pick, instead adds damage against targets already at maximum Rust.
augment: Ichorous Glaive heals on every unit kill and much more on an Earth Shatter execution.
Feng Mao led the lobby in healing, which fits, though healing is not split by source.
Imperial Duelist, the more common pick, trades that sustain for a damage and damage-reduction debuff.
crest: Ortus grants speed and power, and takedowns inside that window add permanent power.
It is a gank and chase tool for a jungler who wants to snowball off kills.
improvement: Keep the core; every Fangtooth and both Primes went our way with it.
The real choice is the Eternal at draft: Peal when Earth Shatter opens fights, Fracture when fights run long.
Pick by which kind of fight the draft promises, not by this result alone.

matchup: Gideon was their highest hero-damage player, with Black Hole's drag and a tether that roots.
The Fey killed Gideon early, never died, and out-damaged everyone in the lobby.
Gideon's two kills landed on Bayle and Feng Mao, not The Fey.
build: Combustion, Wraith Leggings and Caustica stack burst and magical penetration.
Spellbreaker's magical armor made The Fey the only ally itemized against Gideon.
The common winning third item is Megacosm, health-based damage over time.
eternal: Vesh adds a damage-over-time that grows with game time; Mind Rot adds current-health damage to it.
Tithe of Death had thirteen takedowns to feed on.
This is the common default pairing, and nothing here argues against it.
augment: Wild Growth gives Bramble Patch more range, which is safety for a mage.
Natural Infusion, stacking ability haste on Harvest Nettles hits, is the alternative for longer fights.
crest: Epoch's brief stasis answers a committed dive such as Grux's Stampede or Terra's charge.
The Fey cannot act while it lasts; use it so the enemy spends control on nothing.
improvement: Keep Spellbreaker while a mage like Gideon is the main enemy damage; it was our only magical armor.
If the next lineup has more health and less magical armor, Megacosm in place of Caustica swaps penetration for health-based damage.
This match gave no reason to swap.

matchup: Terra built all physical armor, and Tainted Guard cuts healing on any hero basic-attacking Terra.
Highland Hurl slows and shreds physical armor, or roots when empowered.
Terra killed Bayle four times; Bayle killed Terra once.
build: Tainted Guard cuts the lifesteal and Dire Howl's omnivamp while Bayle swings at Terra.
Bayle plays best on Grux and Ikra, who died to Bayle five times between them.
eternal: Weald's true damage ignores Terra's armor.
Dryad's Boon does the same job as Ashbringer; Skull Crusher and Kingslayer trigger Wind-Rider.
Natural Resistance is the draft alternative if roots keep ending trades.
augment: Frenzied Fighter keeps Berserk on with no timer while Bayle stays under the health threshold.
That rewards fighting while hurt, which is also when a root or burst finishes the trade.
crest: Iceskorn Talons drops an ice sheet that buffs allies and slows enemies on it.
It is a group-fight tool more than a lane-duel one.
improvement: If Terra's sustain keeps winning the lane trades, compare Tainted Blade against Sky Splitter.
Tainted Blade adds a healing cut and health, giving up current-health damage and lifesteal.
Treat it as a test for the next Terra lane, not a proven fix.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Muriel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Alacrity shield+AS → Consecrated Ground bubble → Reversal global save
ourKits.winCondition: keep the carry alive with global shields and enable their damage
ourKits.passive: abilities grant Sentinel to allies; on-hit bonus
ourKits.playAgainst: she has no damage threat — dive her carry through the shields or pick her first

ourKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
ourKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
ourKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
ourKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

ourKits.combo: Reaping Dash → Hamstring slows → Safeguard spellshield → Earth Shatter execute
ourKits.winCondition: trade with the spellshield up and execute low targets with Earth Shatter
ourKits.passive: permanent power on unique hero takedowns
ourKits.playWith: setup that holds a target for the execute
ourKits.playAgainst: bait Safeguard's spellshield before committing the key CC

ourKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Harvest Nettles stacks → Untamed Growth DoT → Fly Trap pull ult
ourKits.winCondition: Fly Trap a clumped team and detonate AoE on the pull
ourKits.passive: takedowns spawn growths + grant move speed
ourKits.playWith: engage that clumps for her Fly Trap
ourKits.playAgainst: spread out vs the pull; she's squishy — dive her

ourKits.combo: Skull Crusher gap-close → Dire Howl slow → Cursed Edge → Kingslayer knockback dash, Berserk at low HP
ourKits.winCondition: engage, drop low into Berserk and out-brawl
ourKits.playWith: follow-up while he commits the dive
ourKits.playAgainst: his Berserk rewards low HP — burst him fully or disengage; anti-heal helps

enemyKits.combo: Wild Rush charge → Ruthless Assault → Highland Hurl slow → Unstoppable Force cleanse ult
enemyKits.winCondition: engage Unstoppable and grind with Hersir-empowered swings
enemyKits.passive: Hersir stacks empower the next basic
enemyKits.playAgainst: save CC for after Unstoppable Force; kite her charge

enemyKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
enemyKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
enemyKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
enemyKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Old Rusty slow → Gag Grenade silence → Rad Rounds basics → Shrapnel Cannon armor shred
enemyKits.winCondition: kite back, stack Wastelander bleed and Rad Rounds, melt from range
enemyKits.playWith: peel and frontline so he can free-fire
enemyKits.playAgainst: low mobility — dive him or break LoS through his poke; he folds to hard engage

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 5 effects on one trigger: Nyr Warboots, Krix, Voracity, Cannibalism, Iron Resolve. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Tainted Guard, Elafrost, Gaia Greaves.
The Eternal was part of it: Krix (Voracity + Cannibalism) sits on the same trigger as the items (kept alive in fights), so every extra second in a fight made them harder to kill.
Countered? 0 of the 1 players Terra killed built physical armor. We killed Terra 4 times.
Copy it? Krix (Voracity + Cannibalism): 43.7% in 970 Terra offlane games, below the hero's 47.2%. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

card.lesson: Unstoppable Force came back about every 90s instead of 120s by the end (25% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.

fedBy: Tithe of Death (minor): Takedowns restore 15% Max Mana and permanently grant 2 Ability Haste, up to 30 Ability Haste.
Nature's Vengeance (passive): Each time The Fey achieves a Takedown she spawns an Untamed Growth from the Enemy Hero's corpse and gains 30% movement speed for 3s.
lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Never died in 27 minutes, fewer deaths than about 95% of The Fey mid players this patch. The build added health and armor and healing off damage.
Lesson: takedowns were the fuel. Each one The Fey touched shortened Fly Trap, so feeding early made it come back faster (about 66s late); fight right after Fly Trap is spent.
Fly Trap at rank 3: 95s base, about 66s by the end (31% shorter) from 44 ability haste: Spellbreaker 10, Epoch 8, Tithe of Death (minor) 26.
Tithe of Death (minor): 2 per takedown, 13 takedowns.
13 takedowns (4 kills, 9 assists) fed: Tithe of Death (minor), Nature's Vengeance (passive).
The Fey dealt 24,870 hero damage, 31% of their team's, with +365 magical power from items.

Penetration: Combustion 9, Wraith Leggings 11, Caustica ignores 35%; against Terra (level 15: about 55 magical armor, 16 after penetration; took 7,072 magical damage from heroes, 32% of all hero damage they took) and Grux (level 13: about 51 magical armor, 13 after penetration; took 9,771 magical damage from heroes, 42% of all hero damage they took) that is about 34% and 34% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Combustion (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 50 (+18%) Damage to the Target and nearby Enemies.
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Caustica (item): On dealing Ability Damage to a Hero: While they are above 50% Health. For every point of Bonus Magical Armor they possess. Deal 0.2% more Damage.
Vesh (Eternal): Ability damage dealt to Enemy Heroes deals 7% (+0.4% a minute, about 17.8% by the end) of that damage as a DoT over 3s.
Mind Rot (Eternal minor): The major also deals 2% of the target's current health as bonus damage.
Sustain: Spellbreaker: Gain a Spell Shield that blocks the next Ability.; 3,613 healing recorded.
Toughness: +40 magical armor; took 15,960 damage, mitigated 8,510, died 0 times.

Lesson: The Fey's penetration cut through: Terra took about 34% more magical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 15 their armor was about 55, about 16 after 20 flat + 35% penetration).

(changes Bramble Patch, 6.9s cooldown with their haste) Field: 51.5% in 8393 games, 59% of picks, level the hero-role's 51.7%.

(game text: Takedowns restore 15% Max Mana and permanently grant 2 Ability Haste, up to 30 Ability Haste.) Field: 50.6% in 4895 games, 59% of picks, below the hero-role's 51.7%.

Loadout minor Mind Rot: Your Vesh burn also deals damage based on the target's current health, so your spells hurt healthy, tanky heroes more. (game text: The major also deals 2% of the target's current health as bonus damage.) Field: 50.4% in 6737 games, 81% of picks, below the hero-role's 51.7%.

Loadout crest Epoch: Your panic button. When divers jump you, freeze yourself to wait out their burst until your team helps. (game text: Stasis Device:  Enter Stasis for 2.5s.) Field: 51.8% in 9808 games, 69% of picks, level the hero-role's 51.7%.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 5 effects on one trigger: Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Caustica, Vesh, Mind Rot. The Fey has 4 damaging abilities (Untamed Growth, Bramble Patch hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 44 ability haste brought them back 31% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Kept alive in fights): 2 effects on one trigger: Caustica, Spellbreaker. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
The Eternal was part of it: Vesh (Tithe of Death + Mind Rot) sits on the same trigger as the items (every ability hit set off), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 0 of the 4 players The Fey killed built magical armor. Anti-heal on Terra, Gideon, Drongo. We killed The Fey 0 times.

Copy it? Vesh (Tithe of Death + Mind Rot): 50.6% in 4,584 The Fey midlane games, below the hero's 51.7%; this 3-item core: 54.1% in 231 games, level with the 54.9% of that hero-role's cores. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.
